title: The Vigenère Cipher
description: A fast breakdown of The Vigenère Cipher for builders.

hook.text: For 300 years, one cipher was called 'le chiffre indéchiffrable' — the unbreakable cipher.

buildup.text: The Vigenère cipher uses a keyword to shift each letter by a different amount, defeating simple frequency analysis.

discovery.text: Instead of one shift, each letter in the keyword creates a different shift. The pattern repeats with the keyword.

twist.text: In 1863, Friedrich Kasiski found a way to crack it by detecting repeating keyword patterns in the text.

climax.text: The 'unbreakable' cipher lasted three centuries. Every cipher eventually falls to a cleverer analyst.

punchline.text: Three centuries unbroken. Then someone found the pattern.

quiz.question: Why was the Vigenère cipher harder to break than the Caesar cipher?
options: It uses multiple shifting values based on a keyword
It used numbers instead of letters
It was written in a different language
